public_rationale: On August 5, 2026, Goldman Sachs estimated nearly $500 billion in AI-related debt issuance for the year to date across the broader AI ecosystem [e1]. Wood Mackenzie’s October 28, 2026 release reported 54 GW added to the US pipeline during Q2 2026 and nearly 80 GW under construction [e2]. These figures do not establish completion of the specified 190 GW cohort or the annual bank financing necessary to build it [e1] [e2].
limitations: The claim supplies no deadline or annual measurement window.
The packet lacks completion records and a financing reconciliation for the original 190 GW cohort.
The broader AI borrowing estimate does not isolate bank financing for that cohort.
Observed borrowing alone cannot establish necessity. Refinancing, equity, internal cash, and project changes must also be accounted for.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: For the planned data centers to get built, banks would have to issue $500 billion to $1 trillion of data center debt a year, compared with roughly $250 billion today.
conditions: for the planned data centers to be built

statement.excerpt: They will, to actually make these data centers happen, have to start issuing anywhere from $500 billion to a trillion a year.

from_speaker: to actually make these data centers happen
$500 billion to a trillion a year
our_interpretation: “They” refers to banks arranging or supplying data-center debt financing.
“These data centers” refers to the 190GW pipeline identified in the preceding sentences.
The claim asserts a necessary annual financing level, not merely that issuance might reach that level.
No deadline or number of financing years is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Completion of the identified buildout, together with project financing records, establishes that annual bank-arranged or bank-supplied debt of USD 500 billion–1 trillion was necessary.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The identified buildout is completed with annual issuance below USD 500 billion, or comprehensive financing records otherwise establish a necessary annual amount outside the stated range.

evidence.locator: Transcript, Amanda Lynam's discussion of year-to-date issuance
evidence.explanation: This estimate resembles the claim's lower threshold but covers broader AI borrowing. It does not show that the specified projects were completed or required this financing.
The construction update distinguishes development from completed capacity. Its US pipeline is not the original Sightline cohort and cannot establish the antecedent.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Completion records and comprehensive financing records for the original 190 GW cohort, separating annual new bank-arranged or bank-supplied debt from refinancing, equity, and internal cash. These must establish whether $500 billion to $1 trillion annually was necessary. Completion with annual issuance below $500 billion, or a demonstrated necessary amount outside the range, would contradict the claim.
